## Enterotype classification of antibiotic recency cohort

```{r load.lib}
library(DirichletMultinomial)
library(S4Vectors)
library(stats4)
library(BiocGenerics)
library(ggplot2)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(dplyr)
```

If DMM not installed, install it.

```{r install.dmm}
# if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
#     install.packages("BiocManager")
# 
# BiocManager::install("DirichletMultinomial")
```

Next, let's read in our data. 

```{r read.data}
counts = read.csv('data/rh_abx_cohort_rarefied_counts.csv',
                  colClasses = c(X = "character"))

names(counts)[1] <- "public_client_id"

rownames(counts) <- counts$public_client_id
counts$public_client_id <- NULL
counts_matrix <- as.matrix(counts)
```

```{r enterotypes}
fit <- readRDS("data/harmonized_abx_users_dmm_fit.rds")
bic  <- sapply(fit, BIC)
plot(bic, type="b", xlab="Number of Dirichlet Components", ylab="Model Fit")
```


```{r choose.min}
best_fit <- fit[[4]]
```

# assign clusters for our script run

```{r}
# Sample-level cluster assignments
clusters <- apply(mixture(best_fit), 1, which.max)
result_df <- data.frame(sample = rownames(counts), cluster = clusters) # clusters
#result_df$mixture_probs <- mixture(best_fit)                           # probs
write.csv(result_df,
          "data/dmm_clusters_mixture_probs_arivale_abx_recency_cohort.csv")
```

Let's look at the histogram of cluster probabilities. 

```{r histogram.probs}
#hist(result_df$mixture_probs[,4]) # Cool! all look p binary to me :D
```

Look at feature weights.

```{r}
# Feature (taxon) weights per cluster
feature_weights <- as.data.frame(fitted(best_fit))
colnames(feature_weights) <- c("c1", "c2", "c3", "c4")
#write.csv(feature_weights, "data/dmm_feature_weights_arivale_abx.csv")
```

```{r heatmap.feat.weights}
feature_matrix <- as.matrix(feature_weights)
heatmap(feature_matrix)
```
Let's subset to find the most important features

```{r}
df_long <- feature_weights |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  pivot_longer(
    -feature,
    names_to = "cluster",
    values_to = "weight"
  )

df_long |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  slice_max(weight, n = 15) |>
   dplyr::arrange(cluster, desc(weight))
```

```{r}
top_df_long <- df_long |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  slice_max(weight, n = 15) |>
  ungroup()

top_features <- unique(top_df_long$feature) # select features
top_df <- feature_weights[top_features, ]   # select columns from large df
mat <- as.matrix(top_df)                    # make into matrix
rownames(mat) <- str_wrap(rownames(top_df), # wrap names
                          width = 30)
```

Okay now calculate specificity

```{r specificity.for.enterotypes}
specificity <- apply(feature_weights, 1, function(x) {
  max(x) - mean(x[-which.max(x)]) # calcs the difference between max and avg of other 3
})

feature_cluster <- apply(feature_weights, 1, which.max) # finds which cluster most associated

spec_df <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(feature_weights),
  assigned_cluster = feature_cluster,  # which cluster a feature is most associated with
  specificity = specificity            # diff between that and the other clusters
)

# This would show the top features for cluster 1
spec_df |>
  dplyr::filter(assigned_cluster == 1) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(specificity))

# Select top 10 features for each cluster
top_distinguishing <- spec_df |>
  group_by(assigned_cluster) |>
  slice_max(specificity, n = 10)

# Find all features that were in this top 10
features <- top_distinguishing$feature

mat <- as.matrix(feature_weights[features, ])
rownames(mat) <- stringr::str_wrap(rownames(mat), 30)

# row-wise z-score scaling
mat_scaled <- t(scale(t(mat)))

Heatmap(
  mat_scaled,
  name = "Z-score",
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  row_names_side = "left",
  row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 6),
  row_names_max_width = grid::unit(12, "cm")
)
```

```{r assign.entero.labels}
result_df <- result_df %>%
  mutate(
    enterotype = case_when(
      cluster == 1 ~ "Bac1",
      cluster == 2 ~ "Rum",
      cluster == 3 ~ "Bac2",
      cluster == 4 ~ "Prev"
    )
  )
```

Okay let's import the relative abundance data to check the same taxa that Tom did

```{r import.rel.ab}
rel_ab = read.csv('data/rh_abx_data_rel_abundance.csv',
                  colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Merge df
entero_rel_ab <- merge(result_df, rel_ab, by.x = "sample", by.y = "public_client_id")
```

```{r toms.plot.params}
# will re-order so this matches Tom's plots
entero_rel_ab$enterotype <- factor(entero_rel_ab$enterotype,
                                   levels = c("Bac1", "Rum", "Bac2", "Prev"))

color_scheme=c(
  "Prev"="yellowgreen",
  "Rum"="orange",
  "Bac1"="#088888",
  "Bac2"="#A280AE"
)
```

```{r prevotella}
prev = ggplot(entero_rel_ab,
           aes(enterotype, Bacteria_Bacteroidetes_Bacteroidia_Bacteroidales_Prevotellaceae_Prevotella_9,
               fill=factor(enterotype))) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_scheme) + 
  stat_boxplot(geom = "errorbar", width = .5) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .4) +
  theme(text=element_text(size=14)) + 
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  labs(y = "Prevotella_9") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# ggsave("prevotella.pdf", width = 4, height = 4)
```




```{r plot.rum}
rum = ggplot(entero_rel_ab,
             aes(enterotype, Bacteria_Firmicutes_Clostridia_Clostridiales_Ruminococcaceae_Ruminococcus_2,
                 fill=factor(enterotype)))+
```

```{r stitch.together}
library(patchwork)
(bacteroides + prev) / (faecali + rum)
```
